method: Each listed item was read with its stem, all options, keyed answer(s), explanations and takeaway. Statuses are manually reasoned, not inferred from a schema or automated pass rule.
limitations: Independent AI editorial/clinical-reasoning screen; not external clinician validation or psychometric validation.
Pass applies only to the recorded content hash. New or changed content requires further review.
No comparison against proprietary examination items; originality judged from author provenance and item content.
Cross-bank learning-objective overlap remains provisional until all batches are available.
Source checks below support only the explicitly associated claims; other category references are general reading unless specifically verified.

sourceChecks.limitation: Supports this general nutrition claim, not an individualized anemia treatment plan.

items.assessment: Established routine wound skills make warning-sign/contact teaching the remaining demonstrated safety need. Other options are legitimate discharge teaching but lower priority here.
Caregiving timing is a concrete adherence barrier distinguished from access, packaging and adverse effects by relevant client data. The shorter key is not cued by comprehensiveness.
Mechanical packaging difficulty, absent helper and independence preference make adaptation assessment preferable to service takeover. Reasoning is now case-specific.

issues: An appropriate syringe for0.5mL would ordinarily be a small device on which5mL cannot be drawn; the tenfold scenario needs a physically coherent measurement setup.
proposedChanges: Use a verbal error: the caregiver reads the prescribed0.5mL aloud as5mL, then ask for a response that checks interpretation and guides correct demonstration. Alternatively show an actual scale with a feasible error. Adjust chosen-marking wording if no marking was selected.

items.assessment: Conflicting service instructions and inability to identify first task justify a coordinated action checklist; alternatives are credible information-overload responses.
New visual aids and avoided print support assessing visual access before assumed reluctance. Prior knowledge and family support remain reasonable but less targeted assessments.

The SATA asks which questions help judge an app. Asking whether ratings are enough or popularity substitutes for function can itself be useful, so marking those questions false confuses the answer task.
issues: The SATA asks which questions help judge an app. Asking whether ratings are enough or popularity substitutes for function can itself be useful, so marking those questions false confuses the answer task.
proposedChanges: Ask Which findings support choosing the app? Use declarative options: It exports the relevant symptom records; Its advice identifies credible sources; A high user rating establishes medical accuracy; Its privacy terms explain use/sharing of entries; Popularity confirms the intended clinical function. Then keys0/1/3 are defensible after wording alignment. Avoid stating privacy clarity guarantees acceptable privacy; specify the client accepts the terms if needed.
